record.original_question: For the q-coloring model (zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts model), prove uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure and exponential decay of correlations in specific unresolved cases, including q=3 on the hexagonal lattice and q=4,5,6 on the square lattice.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Prove uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure and exponential decay of correlations for q = 3 on the hexagonal lattice, q = 4, 5, 6 on the square lattice, etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be either the hexagonal lattice $H$ or the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and fix an integer $q\ge 3$. A proper $q$-coloring of $L$ is a function $\sigma:V(L)\to\{1,2,\dots,q\}$ such that $\sigma(x)\neq \sigma(y)$ whenever $x$ and $y$ are adjacent vertices in $L$. The $q$-coloring model on $L$ is the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model: a probability measure $\mu$ on colorings of $V(L)$ is called an infinite-volume Gibbs measure if for every finite subset $\Lambda\subset V(L)$, the conditional distribution of $\sigma\!\restriction_\Lambda$ given $\sigma\!\restriction_{V(L)\setminus\Lambda}$ is, $\mu$-almost surely, uniform over the proper $q$-colorings of $\Lambda$ that agree with the boundary configuration on the outer boundary of $\Lambda$.

Prove the following statements in each of the indicated cases:

(a) There exists a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu$ for the $q$-coloring model on $L$.

(b) Correlations decay exponentially under $\mu$: there exist constants $C,c>0$ such that for any local events $A,B$ supported on finite sets $S_A,S_B\subset V(L)$,
$$\bigl|\mu(A\cap B)-\mu(A)\mu(B)\bigr|\;\le\; C\,\|\mathbf 1_A\|_\infty\,\|\mathbf 1_B\|_\infty\,e^{-c\,\mathrm{dist}(S_A,S_B)}.$$

The cases to be resolved are:
- $L=H$ (hexagonal lattice) with $q=3$;
- $L=\mathbb{Z}^2$ (square lattice) with $q\in\{4,5,6\}$.
artifact.category_tag: antiferromagnetic Potts / proper colorings of lattices
artifact.status_search_result: The cases listed remain open in their full strength. Uniqueness with exponential decay for proper $q$-colorings on $\mathbb Z^2$ is known via Dobrushin-type arguments only for $q$ sufficiently large (e.g., $q>2r$ where $r$ is the maximum coordination), covering $q\ge 7$ on $\mathbb Z^2$ but not $q=4,5,6$. For the 3-coloring on the hexagonal lattice, only Monte Carlo evidence of disorder at all temperatures is available, with no rigorous proof of uniqueness and exponential decay. Recent rigorous progress on antiferromagnetic Potts models has focused on trees and on power-law (critical) decay rather than these specific planar cases.

status_evidence.title: The 3-State Potts Antiferromagnet on the Hexagonal Lattice
status_evidence.snippet: The 3-state hexagonal-lattice Potts antiferromagnet ... studied via Monte Carlo simulation, and the model is disordered at all temperatures T≥0.
status_evidence.claim: For 3-coloring on the hexagonal lattice, only numerical (Monte Carlo) evidence of disorder is available.

status_evidence.title: Absence of phase transition for antiferromagnetic Potts models via the Dobrushin uniqueness theorem
status_evidence.snippet: The q-state Potts antiferromagnet on a lattice of maximum coordination number r exhibits exponential decay of correlations uniformly at all temperatures whenever q>2r.
status_evidence.claim: Dobrushin-type results give uniqueness/exponential decay only when q exceeds twice the coordination number, which excludes q=4,5,6 on Z^2.

status_evidence.title: Power law decay at criticality for the q-state antiferromagnetic Potts model
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishes power-law (not exponential) behavior at zero temperature for some planar antiferromagnetic Potts models.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress concerns critical/power-law behavior, not the conjectured exponential decay regime in the indicated cases.
